patient_information: A 25-year-old woman from Bani Suwaif in Upper Egypt (115 km south of Cairo).
chief_complaint: Severe diarrhoea for 2 months accompanied by weight loss of about 15 kg and amenorrhoea.
history_of_present_illness: Symptoms started with stomach rumbles and colicky abdominal pain, followed by anorexia and vomiting; the diarrhoea is voluminous, not related to meals, occurring five to ten times in 24 hours during the day and night; she had received various antibiotics and antidiarrhoeal drugs without improvement, and in the last month developed lower limb swelling and severe prostration.
exposure_and_epidemiology: The patient is from Egypt, where cases of C. philippinensis have been reported, and capillariasis is transmitted through consumption of raw or undercooked fish.
vitals: Afebrile, heart rate 100 bpm, blood pressure 100/60 mmHg.
physical_exam: Generally unwell, pale, angular stomatitis, scaphoid abdomen with borborygmi, pitting oedema of the lower limbs, and decreased skin turgor.
labs_and_diagnostics: D-xylose test showed evidence of malabsorption, and stool microscopy revealed numerous helminth ova (Fig. 58.1); laboratory results are summarized in Table 58.1, showing mild eosinophilia, electrolyte derangement, and hypoalbuminaemia.
management_and_clinical_course: The patient was admitted to hospital and treated with Albendazole 400 mg twice daily for 3 weeks, along with oral and parenteral fluids, electrolytes, a high protein diet, and vitamins; numerous adult helminths were found in stool samples during initial treatment (Fig. 58.2), and her condition improved significantly within the first week, with vomiting stopping and diarrhoea subsiding after 2 weeks.
final_diagnosis: Intestinal Capillariasis caused by Capillaria philippinensis.
